title: docs: workspace layering and plugin capability/config clarifications
body:
Documentation-only pass covering three areas where the behavior was
correct but undocumented or only documented outside the code.

## 1. Crate layering, discoverable in rustdoc

The strict downward-dependency layering lived only in `CLAUDE.md`. Each
crate's module doc now carries a one-line `Layering:` note stating its
`kage-*` dependencies, so `cargo doc` shows where every crate sits.

The notes reflect the **actual Cargo dependencies**, which differ from
the prose grouping in `CLAUDE.md` in three places worth knowing:

- `kage-jsonrpc` and `kage-sandbox` are leaves (no `kage-*` dep);
  `kage-sandbox` is still an empty placeholder.
- `kage-mcp`, `kage-acp`, and `kage-plugin` do **not** depend on
  `kage-loop`; they sit at the same layer (core + tools/provider/jsonrpc).
- Only `kage-tui` and the `kage-cli` binary depend on `kage-loop`.

## 2. Plugin config persistence

`kage.config()` and `kage.plugin_config()` return fresh, non-persistent
copies: mutating the returned table does not write back to the host
config or to disk. The module doc and the Lua type stub now say so and
point at `kage.store` (per-plugin, disk-backed) for state that must
persist across a turn, reload, or restart.

## 3. exec / env capability scope

The `exec` and `env` capabilities are coarse, all-or-nothing grants with
no per-resource scoping, and that was not stated:

- `exec` runs any binary on `PATH` with any arguments; the only
  constraints are a non-empty command and a `cwd` pinned under the
  workdir.
- `env` reads any environment variable, including secrets such as
  provider API keys, and is read-only (no setter).

The capability module doc, the `Capability` variants, the `exec`/`env`
module docs, and the Lua type stub now make the trust extended by these
grants explicit.

## Scope

Docs and the generated `plugins/types/kage.lua` only; no behavior
changes. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`check-ascii`, `gen-lua-types --check`, and `cargo nextest run
--all-targets` (1388 tests) all pass.

title: test(tui): add render-path benchmarks for view::render
body:
Adds Criterion benchmarks that guard the TUI render path against
regression. The render path had no benchmarks, so there was nothing to
catch a slowdown in the per-frame line-building, height/line caching, or
virtualization.

## What

A new `benches/render.rs` exercises the hot path through the full
`view::render` entry point over a representative conversation buffer
(user prompts, markdown answers with fenced code that hits the `syntect`
highlight path, and expanded tool call/result pairs with multi-line
output):

- **`render/cold`** - a fresh buffer each iteration so the height and
  line caches are empty: the full build pass paid on first paint.
- **`render/warm`** - the same buffer redrawn with primed caches: the
  steady-state per-frame cost the idle loop pays at its refresh target.
- **`render/scroll`** - warm caches with a moving viewport: the
  virtualized visible-block path without rebuilding every line.

A local run shows the cache doing its job (warm/scroll ~11x faster than
cold), which is exactly the behavior these benchmarks now protect.

## Dependency

`criterion` is added as a dev-dependency with `default-features = false`
(only `cargo_bench_support`; no `plotters`, no `rayon`) to keep the
build tree small. It does not affect the shipped binary.

## Usage

```sh
cargo bench -p kage-tui
cargo bench -p kage-tui -- --save-baseline main   # record a baseline
cargo bench -p kage-tui -- --baseline main        # compare against it
```

## Checks

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo run -p xtask -- check-ascii`, `gen-lua-types --check`, and
`cargo nextest run --all-targets` all pass (1388 tests).

title: feat(mcp): answer sampling/createMessage via the host provider
body:
## What

MCP servers can issue `sampling/createMessage` to ask the client to run
an LLM completion on their behalf. kage previously answered every
server-initiated request with method-not-found, so sampling-dependent
servers couldn't function. This wires sampling through the host's
provider, behind an explicit opt-in.

## How

- `kage-mcp` gains a `ServerRequestHandler` trait. `kage-mcp` can't reach
  the host's LLM provider on its own, so the CLI injects an implementer.
  The connection's drain thread offers each server request to the handler
  (falling back to method-not-found), and merges the handler's
  capabilities into the `initialize` advertisement. Threaded through
  `McpServerHandle::spawn` and `McpManager` (retained for `restart`).
- `kage-cli` implements `SamplingHandler`: it converts the MCP sampling
  params (messages, `systemPrompt`, `maxTokens`) into a `StreamRequest`,
  runs it against the host's default model, and returns the assistant
  text. Other methods (e.g. elicitation) are declined.
- Gated by `[mcp] allow_sampling` (default `false`). When off, no handler
  is injected and no `sampling` capability is advertised, so servers
  never try to sample. It's off by default because sampling spends the
  user's token budget.

## Notes

- Elicitation is intentionally out of scope here (it needs interactive
  UI from a background thread); such requests stay method-not-found.

## Verification

New tests: handler routing + capability advertisement (kage-mcp), and
sampling run + decline of non-sampling methods against a `MockProvider`
(kage-cli). `cargo nextest run --all-targets` green (1385 tests); `cargo
fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`gen-lua-types --check`, and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: refactor(provider): collapse compat providers into one table
body:
## What

The 15 OpenAI-compatible providers were each a hand-written constructor
in `compat.rs` and a matching `if let Some(key) = lookup_key("<id>") {
registry.register(...) }` stanza in `main.rs` -- two parallel lists that
grew by two edits per provider and could drift. This replaces both with
a single data table. Net -207 lines; no behavior change.

## How

- `compat.rs`: one `CompatProvider { id, display_name, base_url }` plus a
  `COMPAT_PROVIDERS` table (15 entries) and a `build(api_key)` method.
  The 15 near-identical constructors are gone. `caching`/`thinking` are
  `false` and `tool_use` is `true` for all (unchanged from before, and
  baked into `build()` since they were uniform).
- `main.rs`: the 15 registration stanzas collapse to one loop over
  `COMPAT_PROVIDERS`. Adding a provider is now a single table entry.
- `examples/hello.rs` looks providers up in the table.
- A new test asserts every `COMPAT_PROVIDERS` id has an `env_var_for`
  mapping, so the table and the credential env-var list can't silently
  drift.

## Verification

`cargo nextest run --all-targets` green (1381 tests); `cargo fmt --all
--check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `gen-lua-types
--check`, and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: refactor: split the remaining oversized files
body:
## What

Brings the remaining oversized files under the 800-line guideline, in
one pass (one commit per file). No behavior change.

| file | before | after | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kage-cli/src/main.rs` | 1315 | 774 | print-run driver, resume/search/fork handlers, and event printers moved to `cli_loop_run`/`cli_query`/`cli_printing` sibling modules (re-exported so `crate::*` paths and `run_subcommand` are unchanged) |
| `kage-tui/src/cmdparse.rs` | 1281 | 582 | test module moved to `cmdparse/tests.rs` |
| `kage-provider/src/anthropic.rs` | 1092 | 667 | test module moved to `anthropic/tests.rs` |
| `kage-plugin/src/events.rs` | 924 | 504 | test module moved to `events/tests.rs` |
| `kage-plugin/src/commands.rs` | 851 | 562 | test module moved to `commands/tests.rs` |
| `kage-loop/src/dispatch.rs` | 842 | 282 | test module moved to `dispatch/tests.rs` |
| `kage-loop/src/run.rs` | 2066 | 427 | test module moved to `run/tests.rs` |

After this, every non-generated production file is under 800.

## How

- Most were code-under-800 with an oversized inline test module:
  relocating the test module into a `<file>/tests.rs` submodule is
  enough, and the tests reach the parent's private items through
  `use super::*` (a descendant module), so no visibility changes.
- `main.rs` is the binary crate root (can't become a directory), so its
  large handler groups move to sibling modules; cross-module callees
  were widened to `pub(crate)` and re-exported from the crate root.

## Not included

- The carried-over `app`/`input`/`run` test modules are large single
  files (shared, interspersed fixtures). Carving them into per-topic
  test files with a shared fixtures module is a separate follow-up.

## Verification

`cargo nextest run --all-targets` green (1381 tests); `cargo fmt --all
--check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `gen-lua-types
--check` (no drift), and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: refactor(tui): split buffer.rs into buffer/ submodules
body:
## What

`crates/kage-tui/src/buffer.rs` was 1402 lines, past the 800-line
guideline. The bulk is one ~790-line `impl Buffer`. This splits that
impl into read-side and write-side submodules. No behavior change.

## Layout

`buffer.rs` keeps the `Block` enum + its impl, the `Buffer` struct, and
the `ascii_icontains` / `count_lines` free helpers (which stay in the
parent so the impl submodules reach them).

| file | lines | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `buffer.rs` | 272 | `Block` enum/impl, `Buffer` struct, free helpers, wiring |
| `buffer/view.rs` | 504 | read-side: scroll, focus, cache geometry, search, folding queries |
| `buffer/edit.rs` | 299 | write-side: block construction, streaming, fold ops |
| `buffer/tests.rs` | 341 | buffer tests |

## How

- The methods of one `impl Buffer` are split across two `impl Buffer`
  blocks in the submodules; private methods were widened to `pub(crate)`
  so they stay callable across the split, and each submodule shares the
  parent scope via `use super::*` (`#[allow(clippy::wildcard_imports)]`).
- `Buffer`'s private fields and the `Block`/free helpers reach the impl
  submodules as descendant modules, so no other call site changes.

## Verification

`cargo nextest run --all-targets` green (1381 tests); `cargo fmt --all
--check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `gen-lua-types
--check`, and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: refactor(plugin): split runtime.rs into runtime/ submodules
body:
## What

`crates/kage-plugin/src/runtime.rs` was 1480 lines, past the 800-line
guideline. It holds two impl blocks (`PluginRuntime` ~715 lines and
`PluginRuntimeBuilder` ~255) on top of the struct/free-fn preamble.
This moves each impl into its own submodule. No behavior change.

## Layout

`runtime.rs` keeps the `SharedLua` alias, both structs and their `Debug`
impls, `SANDBOX_REMOVALS`, and the `plugin_env` / `apply_sandbox` free
functions (which stay in the parent so the impl submodules reach them).

| file | lines | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime.rs` | 298 | structs, `Debug` impls, sandbox const, free fns, wiring |
| `runtime/methods.rs` | 720 | `impl PluginRuntime` (eval, dispatch, registration snapshots, reload) |
| `runtime/builder.rs` | 260 | `impl PluginRuntimeBuilder` (setters + `build`) |
| `runtime/tests.rs` | 217 | runtime/sandbox tests |

## How

- Each submodule holds a whole `impl` block and shares the parent scope
  via `use super::*` (`#[allow(clippy::wildcard_imports)]`); the imports
  are `pub(crate) use` so the glob resolves them.
- No visibility widening was needed: `impl PluginRuntime` has no private
  methods, and the struct's private fields reach the impl submodules as
  descendant modules. The inherent-methods submodule is named `methods`
  (not `api`) to avoid colliding with the imported `crate::api` module.

## Verification

`cargo nextest run --all-targets` green (1381 tests); `cargo fmt --all
--check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `gen-lua-types

title: refactor(plugin): split spec.rs into spec/ submodules
body:
## What

`crates/kage-plugin/src/spec.rs` was 1714 lines, past the 800-line
guideline. It is the declarative plugin-surface spec: a handful of type
definitions plus five large `const` data arrays (`CLASSES` ~477 and
`FUNCS` ~717 dominate). This moves each array into its own submodule
under `spec/`. No behavior change: the data is byte-identical, just
relocated.

## Layout

| file | lines | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `spec.rs` | 125 | type defs (`Field`, `Class`, `Alias`, `Func`, `Table`, `GatedFunc`, `Surface`), `surface()`, wiring |
| `spec/aliases.rs` | 69 | `ALIASES` (`---@alias` declarations) |
| `spec/classes.rs` | 480 | `CLASSES` (`---@class` records) |
| `spec/tables.rs` | 42 | `TABLES` (sub-table declarations) |
| `spec/funcs.rs` | 720 | `FUNCS` (base function bindings) |
| `spec/gated.rs` | 203 | `GATED` (capability-gated bindings) |
| `spec/tests.rs` | 97 | anti-drift / resolution tests |

## How

- Each array is now a `pub(super) const` in its submodule, importing
  only the spec types it needs (`use super::{Func, Field}`, etc.).
- `surface()` references them by submodule path
  (`aliases::ALIASES`, ...). The single-source-of-truth contract is
  unchanged.

## Verification

`cargo run -p xtask -- gen-lua-types --check` reports **no drift** (the
generated stub is unchanged); `cargo nextest run --all-targets` green
(1381 tests); `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --
-D warnings`, and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: refactor(cli): split tui.rs into tui/ submodules
body:
## What

`crates/kage-cli/src/tui.rs` was 2607 lines, past the 800-line
guideline. It is all free functions (no impl), dominated by two large
drivers (`run_tui` ~416 lines, `spawn_worker` ~580). This converts it to
a `tui/` module directory grouped by responsibility. No behavior change.

## Layout

| file | lines | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `tui/mod.rs` | 113 | imports, `WorkerConfig`, module + re-export wiring |
| `tui/entry.rs` | 424 | `run_tui` entry point |
| `tui/worker.rs` | 589 | agent-loop worker thread + per-turn driving |
| `tui/support.rs` | 673 | session title, bridge, dialog, listing helpers |
| `tui/session_ops.rs` | 635 | fork/clone/new/export/resume/delete operations |
| `tui/tests.rs` | 224 | TUI host-glue tests |

## How

- Free functions move into submodules that share the parent scope via
  `use super::*` (`#[allow(clippy::wildcard_imports)]`); the imports are
  `pub(crate) use` so the glob resolves them.
- Functions called across submodules were widened to `pub(crate)` and
  re-exported from `mod.rs` so the globs resolve and no call site
  changes. `WorkerConfig` stays in `mod.rs` (built in `entry`, consumed
  in `worker`); its private fields reach both as descendant modules.
- `run_tui` is re-exported (`pub use entry::run_tui`) so `main.rs` is
  unchanged. The submodule is named `entry` to avoid colliding with the
  imported `kage_loop::run`.

## Verification

--check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `gen-lua-types
--check`, and `check-ascii` all clean.

title: feat(mcp): add remote HTTP+SSE transport
body:
## What

Adds a remote MCP transport over HTTP + Server-Sent Events, so kage can
connect to HTTP-only / hosted MCP servers, not just stdio child
processes. Closes the "MCP is stdio-only" gap from the review.

## Config

`[mcp.servers.<name>]` now selects a transport by which field is set
(exactly one of `command` or `url`; both or neither is a config error
surfaced at connect time):

```toml
[mcp.servers.local]      # stdio (unchanged)
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "server"]

[mcp.servers.remote]     # new: HTTP+SSE
url = "https://mcp.example.com/sse"
[mcp.servers.remote.headers]
Authorization = "Bearer ..."
```

Existing stdio configs are unaffected (`command` is still all they need).

## How

- `crates/kage-mcp/src/http.rs`: an HTTP+SSE adapter. kage opens the
  server's SSE stream (GET), the server announces a POST endpoint via an
  `endpoint` event, and JSON-RPC messages are POSTed there while
  responses arrive back over the SSE stream.
- The read half (`SseToJsonLines`) strips SSE framing and yields one
  newline-delimited JSON-RPC message per `data` event, capturing the
  announced endpoint out of band; the write half (`HttpPoster`) buffers
  each peer write and POSTs it on flush, blocking until the endpoint is
  known. Both feed the shared `kage_jsonrpc::connect`, so the HTTP
  transport reuses the exact same `Peer`, request routing, cancellation,
  and `roots/list` handling as stdio.
- `McpServerHandle::spawn` branches on the transport; the HTTP handle
  owns no child (`child: Option<Child>`).
- Synchronous throughout (`ureq` + `std::thread`), no async.

## Verification

- New unit tests: SSE frame parsing (endpoint capture, multi-data join,
  comment skip, EOF), endpoint URL resolution (relative/absolute),
  endpoint-wait, and spawn config validation (neither/both transports).
- `cargo nextest run --all-targets`: green (1381 tests)
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
  `gen-lua-types --check`, `check-ascii`: all green.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Newer "Streamable HTTP" transport (POST-with-SSE-response, session
  ids) on top of this HTTP+SSE foundation.
- A live in-process mock-server integration test (this PR unit-tests the
  framing adapters, which are the bug-prone parts).

title: refactor(acp,mcp): extract shared JSON-RPC peer to kage-jsonrpc
body:
## What

Extracts the bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio peer that `kage-mcp` and
`kage-acp` each carried as a ~280-line near-verbatim copy into a single
shared leaf crate, `kage-jsonrpc`. Both crates now depend on it and
import from it directly; the duplicated `transport.rs` / `jsonrpc.rs`
copies are gone.

Before, the two copies differed only in doc wording and mutex-poison
strings while sharing identical `RpcError`, `Inbound`, `Peer`
(write/notify/respond/request/request_cancellable), and the `connect()`
reader-thread loop. A bugfix to the framing, EOF handling, or id-routing
in one was easy to miss in the other.

## How

- New `crates/kage-jsonrpc` (leaf: depends only on `serde_json` +
  `thiserror`, no kage crates), so the downward-only layering holds and
  both `kage-mcp` and `kage-acp` can depend on it.
- `kage-mcp` and `kage-acp` import the peer directly from `kage_jsonrpc`;
  the old `crate::transport` / `crate::jsonrpc` modules are removed (no
  re-export shim). `kage-cli`'s `rpc.rs` uses `kage_jsonrpc::RpcError`
  directly too.
- The peer's test suite moves into the shared crate.

Net: -426 / +74 lines.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --all-targets`: green (1372 tests)
- `cargo run -p xtask -- gen-lua-types --check` and `check-ascii`: green
- No behavior change: pure de-duplication.
